correctness.rationale: The powers h,h² are independent by degree, so their line-bundle sum gives a basepoint-free proper map; the monic chart has inverse from B/2, C/2 and D−(B/2)² when A=1. For fixed actual right degree d the highest d coefficients of the normalized target determine the monic zero-constant inner polynomial: the lower outer powers begin at degree at most (j−1)d, so comparison above that degree determines inner coefficients successively in characteristic zero. For each allowed d and effective outer degree j determined by the target degree, the outer coefficients are then unique. This proves quasifiniteness and hence finite normalization in the octic case. The boundary pullback is V(a)+2V(c). The first image is the plane, while on c=0 and D≠0 the inverse v/u=E/(2D) gives the irreducible primitive linear-in-G cubic. Both images have generic degree one, so pushforward gives [Π]+2[Σ]; E=0 on the cubic gives 8D²G and hence the divisor 2ℓ+m. Each line has two normalization points generically. Elsewhere at infinity the preimage is unique and the local determinants are 1 and 4. For a finite map with a unique complex preimage and injective tangent map, the source local maximal ideal is generated by the target maximal ideal by Nakayama; the residue fiber is C, so finite-module Nakayama gives surjectivity of the local map. Birationality then gives a local isomorphism. This excludes all other singular points. Generally the top coordinate is a_r c_0^r; the effective outer-drop and inner-drop maps have generic degree one by coefficient recovery. The two images have distinct generic degrees unless s=2r, in which case vanishing versus generic nonvanishing of the penultimate coefficient distinguishes them. The tautological powers on the two boundary bundles are h_(s−2)(1,…,r−1) and h_(s−3)(1,…,r); these are the stated Stirling numbers. Independent symbolic replay confirmed the two determinants, elimination, irreducibility test, section restriction and sample degree identities; the global arguments above do not rely on finite tests.
residual_risks: The result is over C, with only the reduced singular locus and Cartier intersection cycles asserted; it does not compute the Jacobian singular scheme, local analytic types, or a full boundary ideal.
